name: Powell–Lealand apochromatic microscope optics
summary: London makers Powell and Lealand built their own high-power apochromatic microscope objective, paired with Abbe-style compensating eyepieces, within months of the Zeiss introduction.
description: Powell and Lealand made a 1/12-inch apochromatic objective to their own formula, with compensating eyepieces constructed on Abbe's plan; the combination was exhibited at the Society's November 1886 meeting.
tier_reason: A particular maker's contemporary objective branch is specialist detail; the instrument comparison remains historically useful. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

date.basis: In his address of 9 February 1887 Dallinger recalls the objective and eyepieces displayed at the Society’s November meeting, hence November 1886.

events.statement: Powell and Lealand made a 1/12-inch apochromatic objective to their own formula, with compensating eyepieces constructed on Abbe's plan; the combination was exhibited at the Society's November 1886 meeting.
events.caveats: The account says new glass samples reached English opticians but does not identify Powell and Lealand as recipients or establish which glass they used.

evidence.locator: pp. 188–189, paragraph beginning During this time; address heading p. 185
evidence.supports: Own objective formula, Abbe-plan eyepieces and November exhibition; samples reached English opticians, without identifying the recipient.

date.label: by 9 February 1887
date.basis: Dallinger’s 9 February 1887 address says he already possessed a second objective of that construction; it does not date his acquisition.

events.statement: By his February 1887 address Dallinger had acquired another Powell–Lealand 1/12-inch apochromatic objective and expressed a strengthened favorable view.
events.population: W. H. Dallinger, a Royal Microscopical Society practitioner
events.caveats: One specialist’s acquisition and appraisal do not establish a sale, routine scientific use by others, or universal adoption.
